channel.title: Kure :: Go Kure
channel.description: A GitOps domain model and layout engine, on a thin Kubernetes foundation. Kure helps platform teams describe a cluster in Go and write it out as plain Kubernetes YAML for GitOps workflows — without Helm templates, runtime controllers, or fragile string-based YAML manipulation. Get Started View on GitHub Why Kure? Building Kubernetes manifests for GitOps can be challenging: YAML templating is error-prone and hard to maintain at scale Helm charts add complexity with their templating language and release lifecycle Raw manifests lead to duplication and inconsistency across clusters Kure answers this in three layers. A domain model says what a cluster contains. A layout engine turns that into a reconcilable directory tree. Underneath both, a deliberately thin Kubernetes foundation hands you the upstream Go struct with its identity filled in and then gets out of the way — so what you write is checked by the compiler against the real API types, not against kure’s idea of them.

item.title: Examples
item.description: Practical examples of using Kure to generate Kubernetes configurations. Mounted Examples These examples include full documentation: Getting Started - The complete cluster-to-disk pipeline in Go: build a cluster, generate the layout, write it to disk Patches - Sample patch files for the patch library in go-kure/launcher Sample Data on GitHub The examples/ directory also holds sample YAML under examples/demo/: app workloads, bootstrap, clusters and multi-OCI definitions. Kure has no command that reads these files; use them for the shape of an input, not as a tested interface.

item.title: API Reference
item.description: Kure’s public API is organized into focused packages. Each package README below is auto-synced from the source code. For full Go API documentation, see pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-kure/kure . Core Domain Package Description Reference Stack Cluster, Node, Bundle, Application domain model pkg.go.dev Stack Test Helpers Generation-contract checks for ApplicationConfig authors pkg.go.dev Flux Engine FluxCD workflow implementation pkg.go.dev Layout Engine Manifest directory organization pkg.go.dev Resource Operations Package Description Reference IO YAML/JSON serialization and resource printing pkg.go.dev Manifest Classification CRD recognition and object scope classification pkg.go.dev Kubernetes Builders Generic constructor, per-kind wrappers and sugar helpers for core Kubernetes and Gateway API kinds; the builder contract pkg.go.dev Cert-Manager Builders cert-manager CRD constructors (Certificate, Issuer, ClusterIssuer) pkg.go.dev Cilium Builders Cilium CRD constructors (network policies and related resources) pkg.go.dev CloudNativePG Builders CloudNativePG and Barman Cloud CRD constructors pkg.go.dev External Secrets Builders External Secrets Operator constructors (ExternalSecret, SecretStore) pkg.go.dev FluxCD Builders Low-level Flux resource constructors pkg.go.dev MetalLB Builders MetalLB constructors (IPAddressPool, L2Advertisement) pkg.go.dev Prometheus Builders Prometheus Operator CRD constructors (ServiceMonitor, PodMonitor, PrometheusRule) pkg.go.dev VolSync Builders VolSync backup/restore CRD constructors pkg.go.dev Utilities Package Description Reference Errors Structured error types pkg.go.dev Logger Structured logging pkg.go.dev Versions Supported-version metadata for infrastructure dependencies pkg.go.dev Compatibility Compatibility Matrix - Supported Kubernetes and dependency versions Kinds and Field Maturity - Every registered kind with its scope, and every field the pinned sources gate or deprecate ArgoCD ArgoCD support exists at pkg/stack/argocd/ but is not yet production-ready. It is not featured in guides or examples. The Flux workflow is the primary supported GitOps integration.
